ai.definition: Simulated realities refer to the creation of highly immersive virtual environments through advanced technologies such as Virtual Reality (VR), which can simulate any conceivable environment or experience.
ai.howItWorks: These systems utilize VR headsets and haptic feedback devices along with AI-driven interactions to provide users with realistic sensory experiences, including visual, auditory, and tactile sensations.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for more immersive and interactive experiences in various fields such as entertainment, education, and training by providing a virtual space that can replicate any real-world or imagined scenario.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves creating VR headsets with high-resolution displays, haptic feedback devices, and integrating AI-driven interaction systems to enhance user engagement and realism.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes designing the hardware components, developing software for rendering environments and interactions, and integrating AI algorithms to create intelligent and responsive virtual entities.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include high-quality display technology, advanced haptic feedback devices, sophisticated AI systems, and continuous updates to improve realism and user experience.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as the technology continues to evolve and find broader applications in entertainment, education, and training sectors, but it faces challenges related to cost and accessibility.
ai.regulation: Regulations are still being developed to address privacy concerns, health impacts of prolonged VR use, and content standards for immersive experiences.
ai.risks: Risks include high initial costs, potential health issues from extended VR use, and the need for robust regulatory frameworks to manage content and user safety.
ai.profitability: Profitability is emerging but depends on widespread adoption and cost reduction in hardware and software development.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments are likely to focus on improving realism through better haptic feedback, more natural AI-driven interactions, and expanding the range of applications across various industries.

glossary.def: A technology that uses software to generate realistic images, sounds and other sensations that simulate a user's physical presence in a virtual or imaginary environment.
The tactile feedback provided by devices such as vibrations or force feedback to enhance the sense of touch in VR environments.

subsystems.name: Visual display
subsystems.role: presents stereoscopic images at high resolution and a wide field of view.

subsystems.name: Tracking and input
subsystems.role: knows where the eyes, head and hands are in real time.

subsystems.name: Haptics and multisensory feedback
subsystems.role: lets the user feel virtual objects and environments.

subsystems.name: Compute and rendering pipeline
subsystems.role: generates and streams frames fast enough to avoid nausea.

subsystems.name: AI world engine
subsystems.role: creates and adapts environments, characters and interactions.

subsystems.name: Power and ergonomics
subsystems.role: keeps the device wearable for long sessions.

buildSteps.title: Define the target experience
buildSteps.detail: Decide which senses must be simulated and to what fidelity, from training tasks to entertainment.

buildSteps.title: Design the optics and display stack
buildSteps.detail: Choose panel type, pixel density and lens arrangement so images focus comfortably at close range.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate microdisplays and lenses
buildSteps.detail: Semiconductor fabs build the panels; precision moulding or etching makes the lenses and waveguides.

buildSteps.title: Integrate tracking sensors
buildSteps.detail: Cameras, IMUs and eye-tracking modules are mounted and calibrated so head and gaze motion are captured with millisecond latency.

buildSteps.title: Build haptic wearables
buildSteps.detail: Actuators, motors and force-feedback mechanisms are assembled into gloves, vests or exoskeletons.

buildSteps.title: Develop the simulation engine
buildSteps.detail: Software renders photorealistic scenes, simulates physics and supports many concurrent users.

buildSteps.title: Train and embed AI models
buildSteps.detail: Generative and behaviour models learn to create believable environments and characters that react to the user.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Headset, controllers and haptics are put together, then each unit is calibrated for the user's eyes and hands.

buildSteps.title: Validate with user studies
buildSteps.detail: Comfort, latency and realism are measured in trials before any product is released.

prerequisites.why: enough pixels per degree are needed for readable text and convincing detail.
motion-to-photon latency below about 20 milliseconds prevents motion sickness.
reproducing force, texture and temperature convincingly remains hard and power-hungry.
full-quality ray tracing and complex physics still need more compute than wearable devices can carry.
creating unlimited interactive environments on the fly is demonstrated only in narrow cases.
untethered headsets need very high bandwidth without adding delay.

pathway.milestone: tethered and standalone VR with hand controllers and basic vibration haptics
pathway.unlocks: training, education and entertainment in fixed virtual scenes.

pathway.milestone: mixed-reality headsets with eye and hand tracking at higher resolution
pathway.unlocks: more natural interaction and useful overlays on the real world.

pathway.milestone: haptic gloves and suits with force feedback
pathway.unlocks: a sense of touch for surgical, industrial and remote-operation training.

pathway.milestone: AI-generated persistent worlds with multisensory feedback
pathway.unlocks: simulated experiences that are hard to distinguish from reality.
